title: Runtime behavior corpus and kernel attribution matrix for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement:
We need a repeatable way to attribute per-request latency and cost to the exact kernel execution path taken by the serving runtime across prefill and decode phases. Current telemetry mixes span-level timing and sampled NVTX ranges but lacks a compact, queryable "attribution matrix" that maps request cohorts (model variant, sequence length bucket, batch size, scheduler policy) to the set of kernels invoked and their cumulative cost. Without this, we cannot reliably: 1) reason about regressions introduced by scheduler heuristics, 2) build routing policies that prefer cheaper kernel pathways, or 3) explain P95 latency spikes to customers.

Goal:
Build a runtime behavior corpus and an offline/online attribution matrix that: (a) collects deterministic signals per request (lightweight context fingerprint, ordered kernel list, per-kernel durations, memory pressure markers), (b) connects NVTX-enriched ranges and trace spans into a single event timeline, and (c) materializes an aggregation pipeline that produces an attribution matrix surfaced in Redwood Console and for use by the autoscaler/optimizer.

Scope and constraints:
- Must be low-overhead for production SLOs (target <1% added p50 token latency).
- Use existing trace pipeline (X-Ray/Jaeger) and Prometheus metric export where feasible.
- Leverage NVTX ranges on CUDA kernels but avoid unbounded metadata in hot loops. Use short encoded tags.
- Support both prefill and decode phases and identify attention-mode variants (flash/legacy/approx).

Proposed approach:
1) Deterministic request signature: emit a short base64-encoded "exec_sig" at request start containing model_id, quantization profile, requester cohort, and sequence_length_bucket. This lives as a tag on all spans and as a NVTX attribute on kernel ranges.
2) Kernel event envelope: wrap kernel calls with a compact NVTX envelope that includes: exec_sig, phase=(prefill|decode), kernel_kind, kernel_variant_id, batch_depth, and ordinal. Name pattern: rw:K:{phase}:{kernel_kind}:{variant_hash}:{ordinal}. Keep each field as short hashes to limit NVTX payload.
3) Per-kernel metrics: add Prometheus histograms/counters labeled by exec_sig, phase, kernel_kind, variant_id, and device_type. Expose: kernel_duration_ms, kernel_wait_ms, kernel_mem_bytes. Use sampling for high-cardinality exec_sig — full resolution for a small sampled percentage and cohorted buckets for aggregate.
4) Trace stitching: extend span builder to consume NVTX ranges and create child spans when an NVTX envelope is present. Use deterministic ordering based on ordinal to create a stable kernel sequence per request. Export traces with the exec_sig tag for downstream grouping.
5) Aggregation pipeline & matrix: consume traces and sampled per-kernel metrics to build a time-windowed attribution matrix (rows: exec_sig cohorts, cols: kernel_kind/variant, cells: p50/p95 total ms and contribution percent). Materialize daily and 15m rollups.
6) Console surfaces: add a "Kernel Attribution" view per route/model showing the matrix, top offending kernels for latency increase, and links to trace examples and PRs.

Deliverables:
- Runtime NVTX envelope and span enrichment PRs (C++ runtime + Python/Go wrappers where applicable).
- Prometheus metric definitions and low-cardinality aggregation strategy.
- A Spark/Flink job (or existing telemetry worker) that builds the attribution matrix and writes to Redash/Clickhouse.
- Console visualization prototype and PRD for operational workflows.

Risks and mitigations:
- Cardinaility blowup: mitigate via two-tier sampling (1% full exec_sig, 100% cohorted/hashed buckets).
- NVTX overhead: keep envelope <= 64 bytes and avoid per-token allocations by reusing small buffers. Microbenchmarks will validate cost.
- Misattribution due to async GPU overlap: include kernel ordinal and GPU stream id; where overlap prevents precise attribution, mark cell as "overlap-unsafe" and fall back to sampled traces.

Success criteria (see acceptance_criteria for specifics):
- Matrix shows stable mappings for common cohorts and surfaces top kernel contributors for 95% of routes.
- Instrumentation adds <1% median token latency in 95% of traffic during a controlled canary.
- Console feature is able to link an observed 99th percentile regression to a kernel variant within 1 hour of rollout.
acceptance_criteria: A compact NVTX envelope is implemented in runtime and used for both prefill and decode kernel invocations (PR merged).
Span exporter stitches NVTX-enveloped kernel executions into child spans and includes exec_sig tag (trace examples available).
Prometheus metrics for kernel_duration_ms, kernel_wait_ms and kernel_mem_bytes are emitted and documented with sampling rules.
Attribution pipeline produces a daily and 15-minute rolling matrix queryable by exec_sig cohort with p50/p95 and percent contribution.
Console dashboard shows Kernel Attribution for at least 3 production routes and can link to 5 representative traces per cell.
End-to-end microbench results show instrumentation overhead <=1% median token latency on canary traffic.
